brute.label: Everyday pair
brute.note: Use two different positions, even when the values look alike.

brute.label: Negative values
brute.note: A negative number can be part of a valid pair.

brute.label: Duplicate values
brute.note: Two copies of 4 can make 8; reusing one position cannot.

brute.label: No matching pair
brute.note: A complete search can legitimately return no answer.

brute.label: Only one number
brute.note: One value is not enough to form a pair of distinct positions.

hashmap.label: Everyday pair
hashmap.note: Use two different positions, even when the values look alike.

hashmap.label: Negative values
hashmap.note: A negative number can be part of a valid pair.

hashmap.label: Duplicate values
hashmap.note: Two copies of 4 can make 8; reusing one position cannot.

hashmap.label: No matching pair
hashmap.note: A complete search can legitimately return no answer.

hashmap.label: Only one number
hashmap.note: One value is not enough to form a pair of distinct positions.

two-pointers.label: Everyday pair
two-pointers.note: Use two different positions, even when the values look alike.

two-pointers.label: Negative values
two-pointers.note: A negative number can be part of a valid pair.

two-pointers.label: Duplicate values
two-pointers.note: Two copies of 4 can make 8; reusing one position cannot.

two-pointers.label: No matching pair
two-pointers.note: A complete search can legitimately return no answer.

two-pointers.label: Only one number
two-pointers.note: One value is not enough to form a pair of distinct positions.

sliding-window.label: Moving total
sliding-window.note: Reuse the previous sum instead of recounting three values.

sliding-window.label: All negative
sliding-window.note: The best sum is still negative; do not initialize it to zero.

sliding-window.label: One-value window
sliding-window.note: A window of size one selects the largest individual value.

sliding-window.label: Whole-array window
sliding-window.note: When the window is the whole array, there is no slide.

sliding-window.label: Equal windows
sliding-window.note: Different windows can have the same best sum.

binary-search.label: Middle value
binary-search.note: Repeatedly halve a sorted search interval.

binary-search.label: First value
binary-search.note: Keep the left endpoint until it has actually been checked.

binary-search.label: Last value
binary-search.note: The right endpoint is part of the search interval too.

binary-search.label: Missing value
binary-search.note: An empty search interval means the target is absent.

binary-search.label: Single value
binary-search.note: A one-element interval still needs one comparison.

prefix-sum.label: Middle range
prefix-sum.note: Subtract two prefix totals to answer an inclusive range query.

prefix-sum.label: Mixed signs
prefix-sum.note: Running totals may go down as well as up.

prefix-sum.label: One element
prefix-sum.note: The extra leading zero makes a single-element query work.

prefix-sum.label: All zeros
prefix-sum.note: A zero sum is a real answer, not an uninitialized value.

prefix-sum.label: Last position
prefix-sum.note: Use prefix[end + 1], even at the final array position.

sorting.label: Mixed order
sorting.note: Insert each value into the sorted prefix.

sorting.label: Already sorted
sorting.note: The comparison can stop without shifting anything.

sorting.label: Reverse order
sorting.note: A small key may need to move past every earlier value.

sorting.label: Duplicates
sorting.note: Equal values remain present after sorting.

sorting.label: Negative values
sorting.note: Ordering works for negative numbers too.

linked-list.label: Four nodes
linked-list.note: Save the next node before reversing its link.

linked-list.label: One node
linked-list.note: The head and tail are the same node.

linked-list.label: Two nodes
linked-list.note: One reversed link changes which node is the head.

linked-list.label: Repeated values
linked-list.note: Nodes have separate identities even if their values repeat.

linked-list.label: Empty list
linked-list.note: There is no node to visit; the reversed list is empty.

stack.label: Nested pairs
stack.note: The last opener must be the first one closed.

stack.label: Separate pairs
stack.note: An empty stack can start another balanced group.

stack.label: Wrong nesting
stack.note: Having equal numbers of openers and closers is not enough.

stack.label: Unclosed opener
stack.note: A leftover opener makes the answer false.

stack.label: Empty text
stack.note: No unmatched bracket means the empty text is balanced.

bfs.label: Winding route
bfs.note: Explore equally distant cells before moving farther away.

bfs.label: Adjacent goal
bfs.note: A goal next to the start needs only one move.

bfs.label: Blocked goal
bfs.note: Exhausting the queue can prove that no route exists.

bfs.label: Necessary detour
bfs.note: Walls can force a longer route than straight-line distance.

bfs.label: Open board
bfs.note: Several shortest routes can have the same length.

dfs.label: Connected corridors
dfs.note: A long winding area can still be one connected region.

dfs.label: Open board
dfs.note: Every cell belongs to one region.

dfs.label: Four islands
dfs.note: Diagonal contact does not count as a four-direction connection.

dfs.label: Only walls
dfs.note: No open cells means zero regions.

dfs.label: Two rooms
dfs.note: Finish one flood before starting another.

trees.label: Balanced search tree
trees.note: In-order means left subtree, node, then right subtree.

trees.label: Left-heavy tree
trees.note: The smallest node can be several left links away.

trees.label: Right-heavy tree
trees.note: Missing left children do not stop a traversal.

trees.label: Single root
trees.note: A tree with one node has a one-value traversal.

trees.label: Empty tree
trees.note: A missing root is the recursion base case.

backtracking.label: Three choices
backtracking.note: Each position has a take branch and a skip branch.

backtracking.label: Empty set
backtracking.note: There is one subset of an empty set: the empty subset.

backtracking.label: Negative values
backtracking.note: The choices depend on positions, not the sign of a value.

backtracking.label: Four choices
backtracking.note: One extra item doubles the number of subsets.

intervals.label: Overlapping ranges
intervals.note: Sort by start, then extend the most recent merged range.

intervals.label: Touching endpoints
intervals.note: Closed intervals sharing an endpoint are merged here.

intervals.label: Contained range
intervals.note: A range inside another does not shorten its end.

intervals.label: Separate ranges
intervals.note: A real gap starts a new merged range.

intervals.label: Empty calendar
intervals.note: There is no first interval to index in an empty input.

dp.label: Greedy trap
dp.note: Two 3-coins beat taking a 4-coin and then two 1-coins.

dp.label: Impossible amount
dp.note: Even-valued coins cannot make an odd total.

dp.label: Exact coin
dp.note: A coin matching the amount gives a one-coin solution.

dp.label: Repeated coin
dp.note: Coins may be used more than once in this unbounded problem.

greedy.label: Busy calendar
greedy.note: Choose the earliest finish time, not the earliest start.

greedy.label: Back-to-back meetings
greedy.note: A meeting may start exactly when the previous one ends.

greedy.label: Long versus short
greedy.note: Several short meetings can beat one long booking.

greedy.label: All overlap
greedy.note: Only one meeting fits; pick the one that finishes first.

greedy.label: No meetings
greedy.note: An empty calendar produces an empty selection.

heap.label: Bubbling to the root
heap.note: A newly inserted minimum rises past its parents.

heap.label: Increasing input
heap.note: Values already larger than their parents need no swaps.

heap.label: Negative values
heap.note: The minimum can be a negative value.

heap.label: Duplicate priorities
heap.note: A heap preserves duplicate items; it is not a set.

heap.label: Single item
heap.note: The only value is already the root.

union-find.label: Two groups
union-find.note: Joining edges does not necessarily connect every node.

union-find.label: One chain
union-find.note: Three unions connect four nodes into one group.

union-find.label: Redundant edge
union-find.note: A cycle-forming edge does not reduce the group count.

union-find.label: Isolated nodes
union-find.note: With no edges, every node stays in its own group.

union-find.label: Self connection
union-find.note: Joining a node to itself changes nothing.

dijkstra.label: Weighted routes
dijkstra.note: A route with more edges can still cost less.

dijkstra.label: Cheaper detour
dijkstra.note: Discovering a cheaper route updates a tentative distance.

dijkstra.label: Disconnected nodes
dijkstra.note: Infinity means no route from A, not a very large real cost.

dijkstra.label: Zero-weight edges
dijkstra.note: Zero cost is allowed; negative cost is not.

dijkstra.label: Equal-cost routes
dijkstra.note: Ties can reach the same shortest distance through different nodes.
